root_idea.summary: The root has two opposed semantic orientations: concealment or imperceptibility, and manifestation or emergence from concealment.
root_idea.development: The concealment branch develops into hiddenness, secrecy, self-concealment, covered things, and things imperceptible to the senses or mind. A contrasting branch denotes appearing, making apparent, bringing forth, or the faint flashing of lightning; the Quranic vocabulary chiefly represents the concealment branch.

senses.definition: To be hidden, imperceptible, or unapparent.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of something that does not become apparent to perception or understanding; Quranic occurrences express hiddenness rather than an act of concealment by an agent.

senses.definition: To hide, conceal, or keep something secret.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use, including concealing information, actions, objects, or inward matters; passive forms mean that something is hidden.

senses.definition: To make something apparent or bring it out from concealment.
senses.usage_conditions: A divergent lexical reading or interpretation attested for the Quranic expression in 20:15; it should not be confused with the ordinary Quranic Form IV sense of concealing.

senses.definition: To seek to hide oneself or remain concealed.
senses.usage_conditions: A reflexive or intransitive construction, commonly with مِنْ, expressing an attempt to conceal oneself from someone or something.

senses.definition: More hidden, more concealed, or less perceptible.
senses.usage_conditions: A comparative adjective in the Quranic expression contrasting degrees of concealment or hiddenness.
The active participle of اِسْتَخْفَى. In the Quranic passage, an alternative interpretation takes it in the opposite sense, “appearing,” as noted below.
An alternative interpretation reported for the Quranic expression in 13:11; the more direct contextual sense is one who hides himself by night.

senses.definition: Something hidden or secret; a concealed matter.
senses.usage_conditions: A feminine active participle used substantivally for what is unapparent or concealed.
Describes something unapparent or difficult to perceive, and by extension an action or manner kept from public notice.

senses.definition: Secretly, privately, or quietly; inwardly and unobtrusively.
senses.usage_conditions: An adverbial noun used especially in prayer or supplication, where it can emphasize secrecy, inward devotion, quietness, or stillness rather than public display.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become apparent or perceptible to someone; to emerge from concealment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The opposite branch of the verb, especially in the construction خَفِيَ لَهُ, and in idioms for what was concealed becoming manifest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something apparent, remove its covering, or draw it forth from concealment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive usage reported alongside the concealment sense; the distinction between the two opposite meanings is lexically disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a voice perceptible or audible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied specifically to making a voice heard, including a voice accompanied by moaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suppress, stifle, lower, soften, or utter a voice faintly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use with the voice or speech; it describes reduced audibility rather than concealment of an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make oneself unapparent, lurk, lie in ambush, or hide oneself from someone; hence, in a reported idiom, to steal covertly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical reflexive use distinct from the Form X Quranic verb; the lexical reports vary in the forms used for this construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flash faintly, said of lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate root branch concerning a weak or slight flash of lightning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imperceptible, unapparent, latent, or obscure thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use for something not readily perceived or evident.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lank in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic description of a man whose belly is slender or narrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hiddenness, concealment, or a secret.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in expressions for acting covertly; a traditional idiom can associate it with what becomes manifest after concealment, or with low ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Low or depressed ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized or idiomatic interpretation of خَفَاء in the expression بَرِحَ الخَفَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A covering or garment used to cover another thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a wrap or garment worn over other clothes and any covering placed over an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A flower calyx or covering of a flower.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually occurring in the plural أَخْفِيَةُ النَّوْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The eyes, figuratively described as coverings of drowsiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression, أَخْفِيَةُ الكَرَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who secludes himself from people or whose place is concealed from them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized personal description derived from the adjective of hiddenness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deep or concealed well, especially one that has filled up and been dug or cleared out again.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for a well whose water or location is not readily apparent, or which has been reopened after being filled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dense or tangled thicket serving as a lion’s covert; also a place frequented by lions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized environmental noun and place-name usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slight taint, touch, or infection of insanity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression بِهِ خَفِيَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A jinn or other hidden being; in an opposing usage, mankind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The jinn sense is explained by their concealing themselves from human sight; the contrary mankind sense is separately reported in the same lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mankind or a human being.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contrary or opposite lexical use reported for the same form, not a general synonym for every occurrence of الخافي.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land inhabited by jinn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a place associated with hidden beings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A feather in the concealed or lower part of a bird’s wing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural الخَوَافِي denotes specified lower or hidden wing feathers, with variant technical counts in the lexical reports.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Palm branches growing below the central branches of the palm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal usage, called العَوَاهِنُ in the Hijaz.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be slain secretly or without the killing becoming known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare reported usage; the source itself notes that it may reflect a transcription of a passive form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw a dead body from a grave in order to steal its grave-clothes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized grave-robbing usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig or clear out a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive usage reported for the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rifler of graves or a grave-robber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle is explained either by extracting grave-clothes or by stealing covertly; it is a specialized noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hand of a thief or grave-robber, taking covertly rather than by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional legal expression contrasted with the hand of one who seizes openly or by force.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers hiddenness, appearing, faint or suppressed voice, and covert hiddenness expressions.
Covers secret or inward خفية, self-concealment, covert theft, and subdued voice.
Covers concealment, divergent manifestation readings, drawing forth, and opposite voice usages.
Rare reported covert-killing usage, with the source’s transcription qualification preserved in the target conditions.
Secret killing without the act becoming known.
Nominal use for an imperceptible or unapparent thing.
Secret or hiddenness sense and the reported low-ground interpretation.
Adjective of hiddenness, secrecy, stealth, and soft or faint voice; also supports the comparative Quranic adjective sense.
State of being covert, secret, or unapparent.
Quran-attested hiding sense and the reported opposite appearing interpretation.

cautions: The expression in 20:15 has divergent lexical readings and interpretations: making the Hour apparent, removing its covering, or concealing it. The Form IV senses distinguish the ordinary concealment use from this reported alternative.
For مُسْتَخْفٍ in 13:11, the direct sense is hiding by night, but a reported interpretation takes the form as appearing; this opposite sense is retained as a qualified Quran-attested alternative.
The report that اِخْتَفَى can mean being slain secretly is explicitly qualified in the lexical evidence as possibly reflecting a transcription of a passive form.
